name: Ötztaler Höhenstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The Ötztal High Mountain and Glacier Road reaches the Rettenbach and Tiefenbach glaciers: the highest paved road pass in the Eastern Alps at 2,830 meters.
preis: Toll road (cars approx. €22; included in Sölden lift passes in autumn)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from late May to late October (weather permitting; winter ski operations)
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Ötztaler Glacier Road (Ötztaler Gletscherstraße) reaches an elevation of 2,830 meters at Tiefenbachferner, making it the second highest paved road in Europe and the highest mountain road in the entire Eastern Alps. Originating from the world-renowned resort of Sölden at 1,377 meters, this engineering feat winds fifteen kilometers up through fifteen dramatic hairpin turns with gradients of up to thirteen percent into the high-alpine glacier realm of the Ötztal Alps. The scenic roadway links the valley first with the Rettenbach Glacier, then passes through the 1,729-meter Rosi Mittermaier Tunnel – Europe's highest road tunnel – to reach the Tiefenbach Glacier. Upon arrival, visitors are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic vistas over deep crevasses, eternal glacial ice, and dozens of three-thousand-meter peaks, crowned by the 3,768-meter Wildspitze.

Route & Requirements

The roadway is fully two-lane, paved, and kept in outstanding condition; however, drivers, motorcyclists, and road cyclists must maintain sharp focus and verify reliable brakes before ascending. Downshifting early when descending is essential to prevent brake fading. Spacious, level panoramic viewing areas at both glaciers are completely barrier-free. At Tiefenbach Glacier, a cantilevered viewing bridge extends twenty-five meters out over a dizzying void. For alpine hikers, glacier parking lots serve as trailheads for demanding treks, such as the path to the Braunschweiger Hütte or the panoramic route connecting both glaciers. Warm clothing, sturdy mountain shoes, and sunglasses are indispensable even at the height of summer.

Visit & Arrival

The glacier road is open from June through November, depending on seasonal snowfall and weather conditions. A toll is collected at the toll station just above Sölden. From mid-June to mid-October, regular public glacier buses run between Ötztal railway station, Sölden, and both glaciers. Holders of the Ötztal Inside Summer Card travel on public buses and pass the toll road completely free of charge throughout their stay.

Tips

Set off early on sunny mornings to avoid midday traffic and capture the golden dawn light illuminating dramatic glacier seracs. Take ample time for photo stops along the scenic road to marvel at the icefalls and the futuristic Gaislachkogl gondola architecture. Stop at the glacier restaurant on Rettenbachferner to enjoy traditional Tyrolean Gröstl on the sun deck.
